speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. To better understand your shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, can you tell me exactly when this pain started relative to your surgery and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the pain when eating suggests possible tragus involvement or nerve irritation. Can you describe the exact location of the pain and whether it radiates to your jaw or teeth? Also, have you noticed any drainage, fever, or changes in hearing since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia post-Tympanoplasty (triggered by mastication and pressure).

Based on your history of shooting pain specifically triggered by eating and discomfort from earrings, this strongly suggests irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve rather than an active infection. Since your hearing has improved and there are no signs of drainage or fever, I will not order further imaging or labs. The treatment plan will focus on managing the neuropathic pain and avoiding pressure on the ear until the nerve recovers. Do you have any allergies to medications, specifically to gabapentin or amitriptyline?
